canonical_definition:
What it is. Most commonly described as Lean's largest community-maintained repository, Mathlib is also treated as the Lean mathematical library that serves as the formal environment for compiling and checking theorem statements and proofs. Papers use it both as a source of evaluation theorems for testing generalization, including newly added theorems in one study, and as the library against which correctness tests are run in a matching Lean and Mathlib setup.

What it is claimed to measure. In the available relationships, Mathlib is not claimed to measure any construct, and it is linked to one behavioral indicator, theorem proving. That connection is reported as a related link rather than a direct measurement claim, with one paper stating that most neural theorem provers based on Lean are primarily trained on Mathlib.

Space of uses. No other measurement instrument is linked to it. Across the definitions and snippets, papers use Mathlib as shared infrastructure: a repository models may have trained on, a source of evaluation theorems for generalization tests, and the formal environment used to compile, check, and run correctness tests for theorem statements and proofs.
